title: One number for all your agents

steps.text: Tomorrow at nine, I demo to Northwind, our biggest prospect. Tonight, I fly to New York. Three agents are working for me: Claude Code on a checkout bug, ChatGPT on our Slack, and Gemini on my email and calendar.
But every one of them needs me at a screen, reading. The moment I leave my desk, it piles up. Claude Code has a question. Slack is filling up. My inbox has news. And everything waits.
On my phone, all I get are notifications. To act on them, I'd have to stop, open each app, and read. Sometimes it's just easier to talk.
I don't want to read. I want to just talk, and get things done, without looking at a screen.
Think about how I work with people. Sometimes I email. Sometimes I chat. Sometimes we meet on video. And sometimes I just pick up the phone.
My agents give me one way in: a screen I have to read. The phone is the first missing piece we'd like to fix.
{{product}} fills that first gap: one phone number for all my agents. I can call it, and it calls me back.
It picks the right agent for each request. It listens, keeps answers short, asks before it acts, and calls back when there's news.
Here's tonight. Before my flight, I'm out for a walk. Phone in my pocket, I call my {{product}}.
Hey. What's waiting for me?
Three things. Your flight is delayed, so let's start there. Then Claude Code needs a decision, and Northwind posted in Slack.
Okay. The flight?
It's delayed ninety minutes, so you'll miss dinner with Dana at seven. Should I ask her to move it to breakfast at eight?
Yes, please.
I've sent her the request, and I'll tell you when she replies. Now, Claude Code. Refunds use the same code as checkout. Should it fix them too?
Yes, but don't merge. What did Northwind say?
Their CTO, Maria, joined the shared channel an hour ago. She wants to see refunds in tomorrow's demo.
Good thing we're fixing them.
Exactly. I'll call you when Claude Code is finished.
I hang up. Claude Code keeps working.

Hi Vignesh. Claude Code is done. Checkout and refunds both pass, all two hundred fourteen tests. The pull request is open, not merged. And Dana replied: breakfast at eight works. The links are in your texts.
Thanks!
I called my agents, and they called me back. Three agents, one number, and I never looked at a screen.
Just talk. Your agents do the rest.
